ranked.headline: Automated pipelines and benchmarks quantify single-cell and imaging data
ranked.summary: Automated preprocessing, benchmarks, and open pipelines now target high-dimensional single-cell and imaging data across recent preprints and papers.

ranked.headline: Graph models integrate molecular networks for drug, protein, and driver-gene prediction
ranked.summary: Recent models inject explicit biological structure, such as PPI topology and pathway hierarchies, into graph learners for disease and drug tasks.

ranked.headline: Evaluation layers for omics pipelines now test computational methods across datasets
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks of transcriptomic pipelines, perturbation models, and integration methods expose how evaluation design shapes reported performance.

ranked.headline: Leakage and bias audits reshape ML benchmarks for molecular and protein design
ranked.summary: Recent preprints release public benchmarks and audit leakage to test whether reported ML performance reflects genuine predictive capability.

ranked.headline: Structure-aware protein models link sequence grammar to 3D design and function
ranked.summary: Language models and graph networks now encode 3D side-chain and domain context to guide binder redesign, ligand binding, and allosteric site prediction.

ranked.headline: Long-read methods infer haplotypes and allele-specific expression from sequencing data
ranked.summary: Long-read sequencing now supports haplotype phasing and allele-specific inference, but accuracy depends on platform, reference, and coverage.

ranked.headline: Linking genomic variants and regulatory elements to functional phenotypes
ranked.summary: Variant-to-function mapping now spans protein structure, enhancer models, and TF binding data, with new bias and colocalisation caveats.

ranked.headline: Mechanistic models tie microbial and Physarum dynamics to specific population outcomes
ranked.summary: Explicit mechanisms such as phenotypic switching, nutrient depletion, and dynamic resource allocation are now linked to defined outcome criteria.

ranked.headline: Generative and representation models for inverse problems in biological imaging
ranked.summary: Pretrained and aligned generative models now restore 3D microscopy volumes and impute missing data across biological imaging views.

ranked.headline: Pretrained biological encoders gain task-specific refinement layers before fine-tuning
ranked.summary: Preprints and papers now add prior-guided, confidence-weighted, and role-aware modules atop pretrained single-cell, DNA, and drug-target encoders.

ranked.headline: Bayesian and stochastic models address missed events and uncertain measurement times
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published study model missed events, stochastic transcription noise, and uncertain sampling times in single-cell and kinetic data.

ranked.headline: Sampling and likelihood layers steer generative models of biomolecular conformations
ranked.summary: Generative and Bayesian sampling methods now target PTM-conditioned, mechanical, and disordered protein states, testing what inference layers recover.

ranked.headline: ML infers tumor molecular states from histology, imaging, and multi-omic profiles
ranked.summary: Histology, MRI, and plasma metabolomics models now yield candidate biomarkers, with benchmarks on held-out cohorts and new spatial transcriptomics datasets.

ranked.headline: Computational screening and generative design target RNA splicing and RNAi specificity
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply genome-pretrained, generative, and chemoinformatic models to RNA targets in splicing, RNAi, and repeat expansion disease.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks expose gaps between simulated and real Nanopore error profiles
ranked.summary: Long-read simulators and pathogen pipelines are now explicitly benchmarked against real Oxford Nanopore and Illumina sequencing data.

ranked.headline: Directed diffusion and agentic search steer biomolecular sequence design
ranked.summary: Recent preprints add explicit multi-objective, directional, and diversity control to generative models for proteins, binders, ligands, and polymers.

ranked.headline: Packaging and dependency tracking for reproducible biomedical software analysis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published study treat software packaging and dependency structure as measurable components of reproducible computational biology.

ranked.headline: Learned embeddings and generative models applied to microbiome and gene-pair prediction
ranked.summary: Genomic and protein language model embeddings now feed set-based, denoising, and diffusion architectures for biological prediction and generation.

ranked.headline: Single-cell and spatial tools infer cell-cell interactions and regulatory dynamics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications extend single-cell and spatial measurements to cell-cell interaction, regulatory network, and cross-species resolution.

ranked.headline: LLM agents convert biomedical literature into structured, computable records
ranked.summary: Agentic workflows now extract assay data, causal evidence, and simulation configurations from papers, with human oversight over the outputs.

ranked.headline: Compact structural encodings infer protein function, phylogeny, and RNA conformation
ranked.summary: Compact representations of sparse or noisy structural data now support function, phylogeny, and atomic-detail inference with explicit uncertainty handling.

ranked.headline: Integrated resources map genes and vesicle cargo to disease and cross-species function
ranked.summary: Fragmented gene and cargo resources are being consolidated into source-attributed, queryable platforms that link molecular annotations to disease evidence.

ranked.headline: Metabolic models fitted and forecast via differentiable and hybrid dynamical frameworks
ranked.summary: Single bulk readouts and multi-species ecological data now constrain mechanistic metabolic models for inference and prediction.

ranked.headline: Metagenomic tools diverge in ARG detection and gain control-free contamination checks
ranked.summary: Benchmarks across 270M+ metagenomic genes show detection pipelines disagree, making tool choice and built-in quality control consequential.

ranked.headline: Protein language models predict immune receptor-peptide recognition and presentation
ranked.summary: Learned sequence models now span TCR, KIR, and MHC-II recognition alongside quantitative HLA-I presentation linked to immunogenicity.

ranked.headline: Neural models of biological dynamics face identifiability and interpretability limits
ranked.summary: Neural inference and learned pre-patterns now test whether fitted dynamical models recover the mechanisms they are meant to represent.

ranked.headline: Computational modeling of isomiR targeting, read denoising, and EV provenance
ranked.summary: isomiR-resolved models now address target prediction, read denoising, and extracellular vesicle origin using public small RNA data.

ranked.headline: Quantifying reliability of computational inference across multiomic and single-cell data
ranked.summary: Preprints now treat analytical choices, method agreement and cross-modal link confidence as measurable quantities rather than fixed pipeline outputs.

ranked.headline: Adaptive time constants, plasticity, and modularity shape neural circuit dynamics
ranked.summary: Recent models implement regulation through adaptive time constants, inhibitory plasticity, and modular architecture to set dynamical behavior.

ranked.headline: Heterogeneous contacts, behavior, and mobility reshape inferred epidemic parameters
ranked.summary: Explicit contact structure, adaptive behavior, and travel now shape how mechanistic models infer transmission and outbreak origins.

ranked.headline: Membrane environments and titratable residues shape side-chain energetics in simulation
ranked.summary: Unbiased and constant-pH simulations now quantify residue insertion energetics and pH-dependent protein states in lipid and aqueous environments.

ranked.headline: Methods address bias in proteomic imputation and genetic association estimates
ranked.summary: Recent items address platform mismatch, heritability bias and Mendelian randomization sample overlap in epidemiological inference.

ranked.headline: Open-source software standardizes QC and annotation across mass spectrometry omics data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints release open-source tools for automated QC, reproducible longitudinal analysis, and glycan assignment from mass spectrometry data.

ranked.headline: Reusable tools visualize pangenome graphs, viral RNA structures and protein modifications
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published tool package variant-graph indexing, ncRNA annotation and lollipop plotting as reusable inspection tools.

ranked.headline: Computational design and docking workflows for ORF1p, aptamer, and peptide targets
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair computational candidate design with explicit reporting of docking failure modes and multi-objective optimization trade-offs.

ranked.headline: Correcting RNA-seq scale bias and inflated single-cell perturbation prediction metrics
ranked.summary: Measurement correction and benchmark validity now determine whether transcriptomic inferences, including single-cell perturbation prediction, can be trusted.

ranked.headline: Physical models of condensate polymers and TCR mechanics probe biomolecular regulation
ranked.summary: An open LAMMPS tool for sticker-spacer condensates and a catch-slip TCR proofreading model add explicit physical modelling this week.
